transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. When can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for a full month. So gentle gardening is fine, but avoid anything too demanding.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information! I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

However, I don't have the specific details about your particular eye gel in my information. I'd recommend checking with your GP or care team to confirm it's okay to start using it again, or checking any instructions you were given at your discharge.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, I'll follow up with my doctor to be sure. Another thing I wanted to ask is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Yes, it is quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That makes sense, thank you! Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after the operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It was about a week ago. I guess I just need to be a little patient and keep an eye on it, like you mentioned. Thank you for answering all my questions! I don't have any more right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's right - give it a bit more time and your vision should continue to improve. It's good that you're keeping an eye on it.

So just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery!
